bill.title: BANNED in Latin America Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 514.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit U.S. foreign assistance to countries in Latin America and the Caribbean that have diplomatic or economic relations with the International Criminal Court if the Court is investigating or prosecuting U.S. or Israeli nationals. The prohibition would apply unless the President certifies that the country has severed such relations or determines that providing aid is in the national security interest of the United States.

industries.rationale: The bill ties foreign assistance to ICC investigations of U.S. nationals, which could affect defense cooperation and security assistance programs in the region.
Organizations focused on international law, human rights, or U.S.-Israel relations have a direct interest in policies concerning ICC jurisdiction and enforcement.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
